defects.description: D1 (unexecuted, source-derived). Other-user staging may not work. Start-AsOtherUser passes the full script as -EncodedCommand through Start-Process -Credential. The encoded command line is about 16.4K chars (P-W05), about 3.5K (P-B11) and larger than 1024 for the squat script. Microsoft documents a 1024-character limit on lpCommandLine for CreateProcessWithLogonW. I did not confirm that Start-Process -Credential uses that API or enforces the limit. If it does, P-W05, P-W06 pre-squat and P-B11 can only end as harness-error or inconclusive, never as pass. Suggested fix: write the script to the shared directory and pass a short -File argument, and add this to the doc as an unexecuted assumption.

D2. Fixture agent recreates its pipe with FILE_FLAG_FIRST_PIPE_INSTANCE after each disconnect (New-AgentServer reuses $FirstInstance). On the AU and instance_allowed fixtures the other user's TryCreateInstance runs right after its connect probe. If that transient instance is alive when the agent recreates, the agent logs recreate_failed_possible_squat and exits 4. Window is microseconds against milliseconds, so low probability, and the criteria read earlier results. It could only add noise to the agent-contact observations. Also, P-W06 client_fails_cleanly_no_fallback is only 'ssh-add exits 2' with no decoy to prove the absence of a fallback.
defects.location: tests/native/windows/InstrumentedAgent.ps1 New-AgentServer and the disconnect loop; Invoke-G03WindowsProbes.ps1 P-W06 criteria

defects.description: D3. Default-mode P-W01 runs 'git config --show-origin --get-all core.sshCommand' without HOME or GIT_CONFIG redirection. This reads the owner's global Git config. The value is recorded in the evidence record and artifact. It does not touch SSH keys, config or agents, and the README does not claim it avoids Git config (the WSL header's 'global Git config' claim concerns changes). A core.sshCommand value could carry owner paths or usernames, and it depends on Protect-G03Text redaction.

D4. Default-mode WSL probes read the owner's %USERPROFILE%\.wslconfig (networkingMode value only is emitted). This is not in the list of protected owner data, but the WSL header says default mode never touches ~/.ssh, agents or global Git config, and does not mention .wslconfig.

D5. The -IAmOnADisposableHost live default_no_override row checks only for names 'config' and 'id_*' in %USERPROFILE%\.ssh. It does not check other keys (for example *.pem), known_hosts, or %PROGRAMDATA%\ssh\ssh_config (an IdentityAgent there would override the fixture SSH_AUTH_SOCK). The row also runs without BatchMode, so ssh may stop at host-key checking before contacting the agent. It is gated behind an explicit owner declaration and recorded only as an observation, so impact is low. The README table should say the check is name-based.

D6. Process hygiene details. keepalive() stops only the subshell PID, not the wsl.exe child it spawned, so a 'sleep 900' session in the target can outlive the probe (disposable target, harmless). Wait-OtherUser kills the other-user process via the Process handle inside try/catch and silently ignores a failed kill (possible access denied). Start-G03InstrumentedAgent redirects stdout and stderr but never drains them.

D7. The WSLENV '/w' flag semantics (include the variable only when running Win32 from WSL) are relied on by the new P-A01 decoy wiring and the env-form row. The research doc cites no pinned source for the flag semantics, and I could not verify them offline. If the semantics were reversed, the decoy would never reach ssh.exe and the harness would fall back to the sentinel pipe set only on the Linux side, so ssh.exe would see an unset SSH_AUTH_SOCK. In that case the Windows default pipe could be contacted by a build that falls back. The unset-variable row has a passive guard; the other rows do not. Label as [U] and verify on first run.

D8. Source-pin hygiene. G03-S21's local snapshot is under /tmp and not committed. The pins file uses id G03-S10 for two different documents (CreateNamedPipe and ImpersonateNamedPipeClient). Both can mislead later citations. Also, running selftest_unix.sh re-creates tests/native/wsl/__pycache__ because it does not set PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE, which reintroduces the stray file the fix removed. I removed it after my run.

summary:
Verdict: the fix resolves every defect and refuted claim in review-g03.json, with no new default-mode path found that reaches owner keys, owner SSH config or any agent. I checked each fix by reading the code and re-running the self-tests and static checks. Nothing could run on Windows or WSL, so every fixed Windows/WSL path is still unexecuted.

**Re-run results (all exit 0):**
- The WSL mechanics self-test gives 4 verified/pass records and endpoint-perms in_progress/inconclusive.
- The PowerShell self-test gives verified/pass.
- The orchestrator on macOS gives 13 blocked records.
- Parse, PSScriptAnalyzer (0 errors, 0 compatibility findings, 56 style warnings), shellcheck, bash -n, py_compile, embedded-script parse and C# compile (PowerShell 7 only), and the verdict/SDDL unit checks (0 failures) all pass.
- 49 records validate against the schema with 0 hash mismatches.

**Status honesty:** all 30 tests/evidence/g03-*.json are blocked with observed_result null and a named missing platform. The only verified records are macOS harness self-tests that carry no requirement IDs and are labeled "NOT G03 evidence".

**Source claims:** I re-fetched G03-S21, the CreateNamedPipe doc, and the pinned authfile.c and w32-sshfileperm.c. Hashes and quoted behavior match.

**What changed in the two major findings:**
- **Git default ssh:** default mode never executes it now. The live row needs -IAmOnADisposableHost and a profile .ssh with no config or id_* files.
- **P-W05:** the redesign uses same-parameter fixtures that differ only in DACL, raw Win32 error 5 criteria, and two controls that turn dependent criteria inconclusive when they fail.

**Newly found, all minor:**
- **D1:** the other-user helpers pass a long -EncodedCommand through Start-Process -Credential. Microsoft documents a 1024-character limit for CreateProcessWithLogonW, and the encoded strings are about 3.5K to 16K characters. This is unexecuted and unconfirmed for PowerShell, but if it holds, P-W05, P-W06 pre-squat and P-B11 can only end inconclusive. It cannot produce a false pass.
- **D2 to D8:** an agent-recreate race, default-mode reads of owner Git config and .wslconfig (neither touches SSH keys, config or agents), a name-based check in the live default-ssh row, process-stop edge cases, an unsourced WSLENV /w assumption, and source-pin hygiene.

**Cleanup:** my selftest run re-created tests/native/wsl/__pycache__/agent_proto.cpython-314.pyc, outside my write ownership. I deleted that file and the empty directory. The harness leaves no processes behind. My console outputs are in tests/evidence/artifacts/review-g03-recheck/.
